name: Roxithromycin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Roxithromycin is a macrolide eliminated mainly in feces (about 7% in urine). Its half-life lengthens from about 12 to 18 hours in kidney insufficiency, but the New Zealand data sheet does not require a dose reduction for the usual short course. Dose is halved in severe liver disease. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The data sheet does not grade kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 300 mg/day (300 mg once daily or 150 mg twice daily) for 5 to 10 days; at least 10 days for streptococcal throat infection (data sheet).
No dose reduction needed for the usual short course; half-life about 18 hours in kidney insufficiency vs 12 hours in young adults (data sheet). About 7% of a dose is excreted in urine.

hd: Dialysis not mentioned in the data sheet. Little renal elimination; no change expected for a short course.
monitoring: QT risk factors (electrolyte disturbance common in kidney failure, bradycardia, QT drugs); INR with warfarin; digoxin levels and ECG (data sheet).

pediatric.usual_dose: 5 to 8 mg/kg/day in 2 doses; 40 kg or more: 150 mg twice daily; maximum 10 days.

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney data; adult data suggest no change for short courses.
